title: Reading checks at moments of change
statement: Place quick are-you-reading checks at moments of change, and keep them literal and answerable in about 2 seconds from the sentence just read.
detail: The Grade 3 inference designs add a layer of first-read checks to the read-aloud: pure literal retrieval, answered in about 2 seconds, placed at moments of change such as a new character, a new place or a key object, with four short options all plausible to a drifting child and only one stated in the text. A built lesson kept the layer, because drifting readers lose the thread at changes, and set each check beside the still-visible text.

// Quick check: one first-read question (who, what, how characters relate), three options, exactly one defensible.

TASK: one quick multiple-choice question that checks a first reading: who is speaking, what is happening, or how two characters relate. Not interpretation. A Grade 9 reader who has read the lines once can answer it.
reading sequences (first-read checks, close reading, analysis, writing)
Most current checks are literal/sequence questions, so a research criticism of interpolated inference is not automatically this case.
Quick first-read FIND MCQs fire at moments of change (each new plant part introduced). FIND only — the answer is stated in the sentence just read; four short options all plausible to a drifting child
And the spot checks across the reading are good: they keep comprehension cohesive across a long text, and they should stay.

Light, literal retrieval checks placed at moments of CHANGE during the first read (a new place, a new character, a key object, a mood shift). FIND only: the answer is stated in the sentence just read.
